ok this is the write up for the outage last night um let me just get it all down. what happened was that at eleven forty p m the primary database failed over and the connection pool in the api didn't notice for about four minutes. during those four minutes every request that needed a write came back with the error connection reset by peer and we served about nine thousand of those. the on call got paged at eleven forty four and had the pool recycled by eleven fifty one so total user impact was eleven minutes.

the reason the pool didn't notice is that we set the health check interval to sixty seconds when we migrated to the new driver and nobody caught it in review. i went back through the pull request and the change is right there in src/Data/PoolOptions.cs, it just wasn't called out in the description.

what we're changing. first we're dropping the health check interval back to five seconds. then we're adding a synthetic write probe that runs every thirty seconds against the primary. and after that we want an alert that fires when the pool reports zero healthy connections for more than ten seconds, because right now nothing fires until requests actually fail.

and for the record none of this would have been visible without the trace we added in march, so whoever argued for that was right.

let me get the readme section down. how it works. scribe listens for the hotkey and starts capturing audio into a ring buffer straight away so the first half second of speech isn't lost while the model warms up. when you let go of the key the buffer is handed to whisper and the transcript comes back a second or two later.

the transcript then goes through the cleanup pass, which is a small language model with a writing style prompt. that pass is what turns raw speech into something you'd actually send to a person, and it's the part people tune most.

known limits. the hotkey is registered globally, so if another app grabbed it first windows gives it to them and scribe has no way to know. we retry on foreground change but there is no way to force it.

audio capture uses the default input device at the time the hotkey fires, so if you switch headsets mid session the first recording after the switch can still be on the old device. run scribe --list-devices to see what it picked.
note: Two author named sections of two paragraphs each, which is exactly the heading threshold; no marker word appears anywhere, and each section is connected prose rather than bullets.

text:
i've been going back and forth on whether we should keep supporting the old settings file and i think i've landed on no. the format was meant to survive the first beta and nothing more, and every time we add a setting we have to write a migration for a shape nobody outside the original testers has on disk. we've had two bug reports in a year that traced back to it, and both of them were people who had hand edited the file.

the counter argument is that a silent reset feels bad, and i agree it does. but we already show the settings window on first run after an update, so a person who loses their preferences sees the window and sets them again in under a minute. that's a worse minute than not losing them, and it's a much better minute than us carrying two code paths through another year of releases.

so my proposal is that we read the old file one last time in the next release, write it forward, and delete the reader in the release after that. if someone skips a version they get the reset, and i think that's an acceptable trade.
note: Three hundred words of one connected argument. Length tempts a model into headings and bullets, and the correct answer is better sentences with no markup whatsoever.
